what: Convert R objects to JSON and back
title: glazelite: fast JSON reading and writing for R
text: Arrays records come back data frames, arrays scalars vectors:
code: library(glazelite)  toJSON(list(id = 1L, tags = c("a", "b"), ok = TRUE), auto_unbox = TRUE) #> {"id":1,"tags":["a","b"],"ok":true}  df <- data.frame(id = 1:2, name = c("Ada", "Grace"), score = c(9.5, NA)) toJSON(df) #> [{"id":1,"name":"Ada","score":9.5},{"id":2,"name":"Grace"}]  toJSON(df, dataframe = "columns", pretty = TRUE) #> { #>   "id": [1, 2], #>   "name": ["Ada", "Grace"], #>   "score": [9.5, null] #> }  toJSON(array(1:8, c(2, 2, 2))) #> [[[1,5],[3,7]],[[2,6],[4,8]]] fromJSON('[{"id":1,"name":"Ada","score":9.5},{"id":2,"name":"Grace"}]') #>   id  name score #> 1  1   Ada   9.5 #> 2  2 Grace    NA  str(fromJSON('{"id": 1, "tags": ["a", "b"], "nested": {"ok": true, "x": [1.5, null]}}')) #> List of 3 #>  $ id    : int 1 #>  $ tags  : chr [1:2] "a" "b" #>  $ nested:List of 2 #>   ..$ ok: logi TRUE #>   ..$ x : num [1:2] 1.5 NA

code: ndjson <- tempfile(fileext = ".ndjson") i <- 0L stream_out(function() {   i <<- i + 1L   if (i > 3L) return(NULL)   data.frame(batch = i, value = c(0.5, 1.5)) }, ndjson)  readLines(ndjson, n = 2) #> [1] "{\"batch\":1,\"value\":0.5}" "{\"batch\":1,\"value\":1.5}"  stream_in(ndjson) #>   batch value #> 1     1   0.5 #> 2     1   1.5 #> 3     2   0.5 #> 4     2   1.5 #> 5     3   0.5 #> 6     3   1.5 total <- 0 stream_in(ndjson, handler = function(page) total <<- total + sum(page$value),           pagesize = 2) total #> [1] 6

title: glazelite: fast JSON reading and writing for R
text: glazelite uses jsonlite’s function names , options implements, argument names, common code keeps working library(jsonlite) replaced library(glazelite). vectors, arrays every shape data frame layouts JSON structure jsonlite’s: nesting, element order field layout. package’s tests check jsonlite. Three defaults differ purpose: Numbers keep full precision: every double written shortest text reads back value. jsonlite rounds four decimal digits default 15 significant digits digits = NA, toJSON(pi) [3.1416] [3.141592653589793] . Missing non-finite numbers written null. jsonlite writes strings "NA", "NaN" "Inf"; na = "string" . read_json() simplifies vectors data frames, fromJSON() . jsonlite’s read_json() returns nested lists unless simplifyVector = TRUE. yyjsonr, fastest JSON package R, makes different trade-: interface (write_json_str(), read_json_str(), options objects), writes differs jsonlite places. default options (jsonlite digits = NA, yyjsonr 0.1.22): glazelite cover jsonlite yet. differences remain: Writing Supported inputs logical, integer, double, character, factor vectors; arrays dimension; lists; data frames types, including matrix, list, data-frame columns. classes, dates, date-times jsonlite::unbox() values, complex raw vectors raise error instead converted; jsonlite yyjsonr write dates strings. NULL written null (jsonlite writes {}), row names data frames written (jsonlite adds _row field non-default row names), lists elements named raise error. Exponents written 1E20 rather 1e+20. valid JSON number. dataframe, auto_unbox, na, factor, always_decimal, pretty options implemented. digits must NA: numbers always keep full precision, rounding implemented. row layout data frame, missing fields omitted, jsonlite. Arrays keep dimension order dimensions length one zero. jsonlite, auto_unbox = TRUE keeps dimensioned length-one vectors values wrapped () JSON arrays. Factors written labels; factor = "integer" writes level indices. always_decimal = TRUE keeps decimal point exponent doubles, integers factor codes stay integers. Reading Arrays scalars one type become atomic vectors, arrays records scalar fields become data frames. matrix simplification: [[1,2],[3,4]] becomes list two vectors, jsonlite yyjsonr return matrix. simplifyMatrix flatten arguments available. stream_in() stream_out() name file argument path, jsonlite uses con. Arrays mixed types stay lists instead coerced character, records nested fields stay lists records.

title: glazelite 0.1.2
text: First release prepared CRAN. exported functions now document return value runnable examples. toJSON() returns object class c("glazelite_json", "json") prints plain JSON text. package logo website https://ninohardt.github.io/glazelite/. stream_in() opens connection yet open , instead re-reading first page indefinitely, rejects inputs neither path connection. fromJSON(), read_json() stream_in() now simplify arrays vectors data frames C++ converting parsed document, makes reading several times faster . Simplification follows JSON structure: [[1], [2]] list two vectors instead vector, array arrays records list data frames, integer arrays containing null stay integer, [{}, {}] data frame two rows columns. stream_in() without handler reads lines parses together; pagesize applies pages passed handler. Data frames matrix columns data-frame columns written one row time nested arrays records instead using first column, data frames whose columns differ length rejected. fromJSON() read_json() now reject truncated documents, input content document, empty input, instead returning partial result. File paths tilde-expanded. Interrupting long write longer leaves output file open; errors interrupts raised native writer released resources. Bundle Glaze headers needed JSON, credit authors third-party code contained Glaze (see inst/COPYRIGHTS).

title: glazelite 0.1.1
text: Write one-dimensional higher-dimensional atomic arrays existing dimension order, preserving singleton empty dimensions without copying. Preserve length-one values wrapped () auto_unbox = TRUE. Add factor = "integer" always_decimal JSON NDJSON writers. Add buffered pretty output toJSON() write_json(). Accept digits = NA full round-trip precision reject unsupported rounding requests explicitly. Add regression checks Stan-compatible shapes, types, file streaming.
